title: Favette Triestine
instructions:
Favette Triestine

Trieste almond sweets in three colors and flavors: vanilla, rose, and chocolate.

Yield: about 36 pieces

Ingredients

2 cups finely ground blanched almonds
1 cup all-purpose flour
3 large egg whites
1 1/4 cups granulated sugar
1 tsp vanilla extract or seeds from 1/2 vanilla bean
2 tbsp white rosolio
3 drops rose oil or 1 tsp rose water
2 tbsp alkermes liqueur
about 1/3 cup finely grated dark chocolate

Preparation

1. Grind the almonds finely.

2. Spread them on a tray.

3. Let them air-dry for 2 days.

4. Preheat the oven to its lowest setting, about 175–195°F.

5. Put the flour in a large bowl.

6. Add a small amount of egg white.

7. Stir into a smooth paste.

8. Gradually add the remaining egg whites.

9. Add the sugar little by little.

10. Add the ground almonds.

11. Mix until light and foamy.

12. Divide the mixture into 3 equal portions.

13. Add the vanilla and white rosolio to the first portion.

14. Add the rose oil or rose water and alkermes to the second.

15. Add the grated chocolate to the third.

16. Shape into small oval bean-shaped sweets with slightly damp hands.

17. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

18. Dry in the barely warm oven for 20–30 minutes without browning.

19. Turn off the oven.

20. Cool completely.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Favette should dry rather than bake, so keep the oven barely warm and do not let them brown.

title: Pinza Triestina
instructions:
Pinza Triestina

Large Trieste sweet yeast bread enriched with butter, eggs, citrus, vanilla, sweet wine, and anise.

Yield: 3 large or 4 small loaves

Ingredients

about 16 2/3 cups strong bread flour, divided
3 cups granulated sugar, divided
about 8 large eggs
1 1/3 cups plus 1 tbsp butter, divided
about 1 2/3 cups fresh yeast
about 1/2 cup egg yolks, divided
about 1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp sweet wine or Marsala-rum mixture infused with anise seeds
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp whole milk, plus 1 tbsp for brushing
5 tsp fine salt
finely grated zest of 1 lemon
finely grated zest of 1 orange
seeds from 1 vanilla bean
1 egg yolk for brushing

Preparation

1. For the first dough, warm a large mixing bowl slightly.

2. Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk.

3. Add about 3 1/3 cups flour and 1/2 cup sugar.

4. Mix until uniform.

5. Cover.

6. Let rise until doubled.

7. For the second dough, beat 1/2 cup sugar with part of the egg yolks and about 4 whole eggs.

8. Add the lemon and orange zest.

9. Add the vanilla.

10. Add about 5 tbsp melted and cooled butter.

11. Add the flavored wine.

12. Mix in about 5 cups flour.

13. Add the first dough.

14. Beat vigorously until large bubbles form.

15. Cover.

16. Let rise again until doubled.

17. Put the remaining flour on the work surface.

18. Add the remaining whole eggs and yolks.

19. Add the remaining sugar.

20. Add the salt.

21. Melt the remaining butter.

22. Gradually work it in along with the second dough.

23. Knead by hand for at least 1 hour, until smooth, soft, and no longer sticky.

24. Divide into 3 or 4 portions.

25. Shape into round loaves.

26. Put on parchment-lined baking sheets.

27. Brush lightly with any remaining melted butter.

28. Cover.

29. Let rise in a warm place for about 3 hours.

30. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

31. Beat the finishing yolk with 1 tablespoon milk.

32. Brush the loaves.

33. Cut a deep star-shaped slash into each top.

34. Bake for about 45–50 minutes.

35. Check that the centers are fully baked.

36. Cool on a rack.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

The long final kneading develops enough structure to support this exceptionally rich butter-, sugar-, and egg-heavy dough.

instructions:
South Tyrolean Apple Strudel

South Tyrolean shortcrust strudel with apples, raisins, pine nuts, toasted breadcrumbs, rum, and cinnamon.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the pastry
9 tbsp softened butter
1 cup powdered sugar
finely grated zest of 1/2 lemon
1/2 packet vanilla sugar
1 tbsp whole milk
1 large egg
2 cups all-purpose flour
1 tsp baking powder
1 pinch fine salt

For the filling
about 4 cups thinly sliced apples
1/4 cup granulated sugar
1/2 cup toasted breadcrumbs
1/4 cup raisins
3 tbsp pine nuts
2 tbsp rum
1 packet vanilla sugar
1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
1 pinch finely grated lemon zest

For finishing
1 large egg
1/4 cup powdered sugar

Preparation

1. Quickly mix the softened butter, powdered sugar, lemon zest, and vanilla sugar.

2. Add the egg.

3. Add the milk.

4. Mix in the flour, baking powder, and salt.

5. Work only until uniform.

6. Wrap.

7. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.

8. Peel the apples.

9. Remove the cores.

10. Slice thinly.

11. Put them in a large bowl.

12. Add the sugar, toasted breadcrumbs, raisins, pine nuts, rum, vanilla sugar, cinnamon, and lemon zest.

13. Toss gently.

14. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

15. Roll the pastry on a lightly floured surface into a rectangle about 16 × 10 inches.

16. Transfer to a parchment-lined baking sheet.

17. Arrange the filling down the center.

18. Fold the pastry sides over the apples.

19. Seal the ends.

20. Beat the egg.

21. Brush the surface.

22. Decorate with any pastry scraps.

23. Bake for about 35 minutes.

24. Cool slightly.

25. Dust with powdered sugar.

Service

Serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

The shortcrust pastry should remain thick enough to contain the apple filling without tearing.

instructions:
South Tyrolean Kaiserschmarrn

South Tyrolean torn sweet pancake served with apple compote and lingonberry preserves.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

5 large eggs
2 1/2 cups whole milk
1 pinch fine salt
4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
4 tbsp butter for cooking
1/4 cup powdered sugar
4 tbsp apple compote
4 tbsp lingonberry preserves

Preparation

1. Put the eggs in a large bowl.

2. Add the milk and salt.

3. Whisk until foamy.

4. Gradually add the flour.

5. Mix until no lumps remain.

6. Melt half of the butter in a large skillet.

7. Pour in half of the batter.

8. Cook over medium-low heat until the bottom is golden.

9. Turn the pancake.

10. Cook the second side.

11. Tear into irregular pieces with two spatulas.

12. Continue tossing until browned on all sides.

13. Transfer to a platter.

14. Repeat with the remaining butter and batter.

15. Dust with powdered sugar.

Service

Serve hot with apple compote and lingonberry preserves on the side.

Chef's note

Cooking in two batches prevents the pancake from becoming too thick and lets the torn pieces brown evenly.

title: Strauben
instructions:
Strauben

South Tyrolean spiral fritters flavored with grappa, vanilla, and lemon.

Yield: about 8 fritters

Ingredients

2 cups plus 1 tbsp all-purpose flour
2 heaping tsp baking powder
1 pinch fine salt
3 large eggs
1 1/2 tbsp melted butter
scant 1/2 cup whole milk
scant 1/2 cup beer
2 tbsp grappa
1 tbsp vanilla extract
finely grated zest of 1 organic lemon
about 6 1/2 cups frying oil
1/3 cup powdered sugar
about 2/3 cup lingonberry preserves

Preparation

1. Sift the flour, baking powder, and salt into a large bowl.

2. Add the eggs.

3. Add the melted butter.

4. Add the milk.

5. Whisk.

6. Gradually add the beer.

7. Continue whisking until smooth.

8. Add the grappa, vanilla, and lemon zest.

9. Rest the batter for 10 minutes.

10. Heat the oil to 350°F in a wide deep skillet.

11. Fill a funnel dispenser with one ladleful of batter.

12. Let the batter stream into the oil in a continuous spiral.

13. Fry for 1 minute.

14. Turn with two slotted spoons.

15. Continue until the second side is golden.

16. Drain on paper towels.

17. Repeat with the remaining batter.

18. Dust with powdered sugar.

Service

Serve hot with lingonberry preserves.

Chef's note

Hold the funnel close to the oil surface to create an even spiral without breaking the batter stream.

Trentino Zelten

Trentino Christmas cake packed with figs, raisins, walnuts, pine nuts, almonds, and candied citron.

Yield: 8 servings

5 tbsp softened butter
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp granulated sugar
2 large eggs
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp whole milk

1/3 cup pine nuts

1 tsp vanilla extract
1 tsp ground cinnamon
1/4 cup rum

1/4 cup almonds or walnuts for decorating

Preparation

1. The night before, cut the figs into small pieces.

2. Put the figs, raisins, walnuts, pine nuts, citron, and almonds in a large bowl.

3. Add the sugar.

4. Add the milk.

5. Add the rum.

6. Stir.

7. Cover.

8. Rest overnight.

9. The next day, add the eggs.

10. Add the softened butter.

11. Add the salt, vanilla, and cinnamon.

12. Sift together the flour and baking powder.

13. Mix them into the fruit mixture.

14. Stir until thick and soft.

15. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

16. Butter an 8 1/2-inch pan.

17. Add the batter.

18. Smooth the surface.

19. Brush with egg white.

20. Decorate with almonds or walnuts.

21. Bake for 25–30 minutes.

22. Cool completely.

Chef's note

The overnight soak lets the dried fruit absorb milk and rum instead of drawing moisture from the cake during baking.

South Tyrolean Krapfen

South Tyrolean rye-and-wheat fritters filled with fruit preserves.

Preparation

1. Put the rye flour and white flour in a large bowl.

2. Add the milk, melted butter, cream, oil, grappa, egg yolk, and salt.

3. Knead until smooth and uniform.

4. Cover.

5. Rest for about 30 minutes.

6. Roll the dough very thinly.

7. Cut into strips about 4 inches wide.

8. Place about 1/2 tablespoon preserves at regular intervals along one half of each strip.

9. Fold the dough over the filling.

10. Press firmly around each mound.

11. Cut out the krapfen with a pastry wheel.

12. Heat the frying oil or fat to 340–350°F.

13. Fry only a few at a time.

14. Cook the first side until golden.

15. While frying, spoon a little hot oil over the top surface.

16. Turn.

17. Fry the second side until golden.

18. Drain on paper towels.

19. Dust with powdered sugar.

Spooning hot oil over the top while the first side cooks helps the krapfen puff properly.

5. Add the eggs one at a time.

6. Mix the buckwheat flour, hazelnuts, baking powder, and breadcrumbs.

7. Add the dry ingredients to the batter.

8. Pour into the pan.

9. Smooth the surface.

11. Test with a toothpick.

12. Cool completely.

13. Unmold.

14. Cut horizontally into two layers.

15. If using, mix the water and rum.

16. Lightly moisten the cut surfaces.

17. Spread the preserves over the bottom layer.

18. Reassemble the cake.

19. If desired, spread 2 tablespoons preserves over the top, taken from the total amount.

20. Dust with powdered sugar.

Cool the cake completely before slicing so the crumbly buckwheat texture does not break apart.

instructions:
Grostoi

Thin crisp Trentino Carnival pastries flavored with white wine, citrus zest, and vanilla.

Yield: about 30 pieces

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
1/4 cup plus 1 tbsp granulated sugar
4 tbsp butter
3/4 tsp fine salt
3 large eggs
1 egg yolk
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp dry white wine
finely grated zest of 1/2 lemon
finely grated zest of 1/2 orange
seeds from 1 vanilla bean
6 cups peanut oil for frying
1/3 cup powdered sugar for finishing

Preparation

1. Put the flour, sugar, butter, salt, eggs, yolk, wine, citrus zest, and vanilla in a mixer bowl.

2. Knead on low speed with the dough hook.

3. Continue until firm, smooth, and elastic.

4. Shape into a ball.

5. Cover with plastic.

6. Rest for 30 minutes.

7. Roll the dough very thinly, about 1/16 inch.

8. Cut rectangles about 6 × 3 inches.

9. Cut two parallel slits in the center of each rectangle.

10. Pull one end of the dough through the farther slit to create the traditional shape.

11. Heat the oil to about 350°F.

12. Fry only a few at a time.

13. Turn as soon as the first side is golden.

14. Fry the second side for only a few seconds, until golden.

15. Drain immediately on paper towels.

16. Cool.

17. Dust with powdered sugar.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Very thin dough and rapid frying are essential for light, crisp grostoi.

title: Spongata
instructions:
Spongata

Emilia shortcrust pie filled with honey, nuts, candied fruit, raisins, cookies, and spices.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

about 1 lb prepared shortcrust pastry
3/4 cup blanched almonds
3/4 cup hazelnuts
about 1 2/3 cups walnuts
1/3 cup pine nuts
about 1 1/3 cups diced candied orange and citron
1/2 cup raisins
1/4 cup plus 1 tbsp granulated sugar
1 cup honey
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp dry white wine
about 2 cups finely crushed dry cookies
1 tsp ground cinnamon
1/2 tsp ground nutmeg
1/4 cup powdered sugar for finishing

Preparation

1. Coarsely chop the almonds, hazelnuts, and walnuts.

2. Soak the raisins in warm water for 15 minutes.

3. Drain and dry.

4. Combine the nuts, pine nuts, candied fruit, raisins, crushed cookies, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a large bowl.

5. Warm the honey until fluid without boiling.

6. Pour it over the mixture.

7. Add the white wine.

8. Mix thoroughly.

9. Cover.

10. Rest the filling for at least 2 hours.

11. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

12. Divide the pastry into two portions, one slightly larger.

13. Roll out the larger portion.

14. Line a 9 1/2-inch pie pan.

15. Spread the filling evenly.

16. Roll out the remaining pastry.

17. Cover the pie.

18. Seal the edges carefully.

19. Prick the top with a fork.

20. Bake for about 20–25 minutes, until golden.

21. Cool completely.

22. Dust with powdered sugar.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Resting the filling lets the honey, wine, and spices season the nuts evenly.

title: Torta Barozzi
instructions:
Torta Barozzi

Vignola flourless chocolate cake with peanuts, almonds, cocoa, and coffee.

2 large eggs
about 1/2 cup chopped dark chocolate

Preparation

1. Preheat a convection oven to 350°F or a conventional oven to 355°F.

2. Line a 6 × 9-inch pan completely with aluminum foil.

3. Melt the chocolate over a water bath.

4. Cool slightly.

5. Beat the softened butter with the sugar until creamy.

6. Separate the egg yolks and whites.

7. Mix the yolks into the melted chocolate.

8. Add the butter-and-sugar mixture.

9. Add the coffee.

10. Chop the peanuts and almonds without grinding them to a fine powder.

11. Add the cocoa and salt.

12. Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks.

13. Mix the chopped nuts into the chocolate mixture.

14. Gently fold in the whites in several additions.

15. Pour into the pan.

16. Smooth the top.

17. Bake for 25 minutes in a convection oven or 30–35 minutes in a conventional oven.

18. Cool completely.

19. Invert.

20. Trim the edges.

21. Cut into squares while keeping the foil attached to the base, as traditionally served.

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Keep the peanuts and almonds slightly coarse to preserve the cake's characteristic texture.

title: Certosino Bolognese
instructions:
Certosino Bolognese

Bologna Christmas cake packed with candied fruit, almonds, mostarda, honey, cocoa, chocolate, and spices.

Yield: 6 cakes

Ingredients

8 1/3 cups all-purpose flour
about 3 3/4 cups diced candied orange
about 3 cups almonds
about 1 2/3 cups Bologna mostarda
about 1 3/4 cups diced candied citron
1 cup granulated sugar
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp honey, plus about 1/3 cup for glazing
about 1/3 cup chopped dark chocolate
1/3 cup pine nuts
1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
scant 1/8 tsp baker's ammonia
scant 1/8 tsp mixed cinnamon, clove, cherry-laurel, and citrus zest
2 cups plus 2 tbsp aromatic red wine for the dough
about 2 cups assorted candied fruit for decorating

Preparation

1. At least 1 day ahead, prepare the aromatic wine.

2. Put about 4 1/4 cups red wine in a container with 2 bay leaves, 6 juniper berries, and 6 laurel berries.

3. Cover and infuse for 24 hours.

4. Strain.

5. Put the flour, candied orange, almonds, mostarda, citron, sugar, honey, chopped chocolate, pine nuts, cocoa, baker's ammonia, and spices in a large bowl.

6. Mix.

7. Gradually add about 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons aromatic wine.

8. Work vigorously until soft but compact.

9. Divide into 6 equal portions.

10. Shape each into a log.

11. Join the ends to make small rings.

12. Leave a center hole that will narrow during baking.

13. Decorate with the assorted candied fruit.

14. Preheat the oven to 320°F.

15. Bake for 20 minutes.

16. Cool on a wooden board.

17. Mature for 20 days in a cool dry place.

18. Turn the cakes every 2 days.

19. Whenever the decorated side faces upward, warm some of the glazing honey.

20. Brush the tops with warm honey.

21. Repeat through the maturation period until the glazing honey is used.

Service

Wrap and store at cool room temperature until serving.

Chef's note

The long maturation period is integral to the recipe and develops Certosino's dense aromatic texture.

instructions:
Emilian Zuppa Inglese

Emilia layered dessert of cake soaked in Alchermes and Sassolino with vanilla and chocolate pastry creams.

Yield: 6–8 servings

Ingredients

about 5–6 cups 3/8-inch slices of homemade ciambella or brazadela

For the pastry cream
2 cups plus 2 tbsp whole milk
4 large egg yolks
1/2 cup plus 2 tbsp granulated sugar
6 tbsp all-purpose flour or cornstarch
peel of 1 organic lemon

about 1/2 cup chopped dark chocolate

For the soaking syrup
about 1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp Alchermes
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp Sassolino or anisette
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp water
1 tbsp granulated sugar

Preparation

1. Heat the milk with the lemon peel.

2. Remove from the heat just before boiling.

3. Infuse for 10 minutes.

4. Remove the peel.

5. Beat the egg yolks with the sugar until pale.

6. Mix in the flour or cornstarch.

7. Gradually add the hot milk.

8. Transfer to a saucepan.

9. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the cream coats a spoon.

10. Divide the pastry cream into two equal portions.

11. Chop the chocolate.

12. Melt it into one half of the still-hot cream.

13. Cool both creams until warm.

14. Mix the Alchermes, Sassolino, water, and sugar.

15. Spread a thin layer of cream in the bottom of a baking dish.

16. Quickly dip the cake slices in the syrup.

17. Arrange the first layer.

18. Cover with vanilla pastry cream.

19. Add a second layer of soaked cake.

20. Cover with chocolate pastry cream.

21. Continue alternating until all ingredients are used.

22. Cover.

23. Refrigerate for at least 4–6 hours.

Service

Serve well chilled.

Chef's note

Dip the cake only briefly so it retains structure during the long refrigerator rest.

14. Cool until warm.

Castagnole Romagnole

Romagna Carnival fritters, soft inside and golden outside, flavored with orange and passito.

Preparation

1. Sift the cornstarch, flour, baking powder, and salt into a large bowl.

2. Make a well.

3. Add the sugar, eggs, orange zest, softened butter, and passito.

4. Mix first with a fork.

5. Transfer to a lightly floured work surface.

6. Knead into a soft smooth dough.

7. Cover.

8. Rest for 20 minutes.

9. Divide into pieces.

10. Roll into ropes about 3/4 inch thick.

11. Cut into cherry-size pieces.

12. Roll into balls between your palms.

13. Heat the oil to 340–350°F.

14. Fry only a few at a time.

15. Turn often until puffed and evenly golden, about 2–3 minutes.

16. Drain on paper towels.

17. While still warm, roll in the finishing sugar.

18. If desired, lightly drizzle with Alchermes before rolling in sugar.

Chef's note

Frying only a few at a time keeps the oil temperature stable and allows the centers to cook evenly.

Bologna Sfrappole

4. Add the sugar.

5. Beat until pale and fluffy.

6. Sift together the flour, baking powder, and salt.

7. Gradually mix them in.

8. Add the orange zest.

9. Fold in the whole almonds.

11. Shape two logs about 12 inches long and 2 inches wide.

12. Lightly beat the reserved egg white.

13. Brush the logs.

14. Reduce the oven to 350°F.

15. Bake for 20–25 minutes.

16. Remove from the oven.

17. Cool for 5 minutes.

18. Cut diagonally into slices about 3/4 inch thick.

19. Arrange the slices on the baking sheet.

title: Panforte di Siena
instructions:
Panforte di Siena

Siena panforte with almonds, candied citrus, honey, and spices.

Yield: 10–12 servings

Ingredients

about 2 3/4 cups whole almonds
1 cup diced candied orange peel
1 cup diced candied citron
1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
1 tbsp panforte spice blend
1/2 cup honey
1 1/4 cups powdered sugar
3 tbsp water
1/4 cup powdered sugar for finishing

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

2. Spread the almonds on a baking sheet.

3. Toast for 5–7 minutes.

4. Cool slightly.

5. Coarsely dice the candied orange and citron.

6. Combine the almonds, flour, candied fruit, and spices in a large bowl.

7. Put the honey, powdered sugar, and water in a saucepan.

8. Heat over medium heat, stirring, until smooth.

9. Immediately pour the syrup over the dry ingredients.

10. Stir vigorously; the mixture will be very thick.

11. Line an 8 1/2-inch cake pan with parchment.

12. Add the mixture.

13. Lightly dampen the back of a spoon.

14. Smooth and compact the surface.

15. Dust lightly with some of the finishing powdered sugar.

16. Bake for 25–30 minutes.

17. Unmold while still warm so the caramel does not stick to the pan.

18. Cool completely.

19. Dust with the remaining powdered sugar.

Service

Cut into thin wedges and serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Work quickly once the hot syrup is added because the mixture stiffens as it cools.

title: Ricciarelli di Siena
instructions:
Ricciarelli di Siena

Soft Siena almond cookies flavored with orange and bitter almond.

Yield: 18 cookies

Ingredients

about 1/3 cup egg whites
1 2/3 cups powdered sugar
2 cups almond flour
1 tsp bitter-almond extract
1 tsp vanilla extract
finely grated zest of 1 orange
1 cup powdered sugar for shaping and finishing

Preparation

1. The night before, lightly beat the egg whites.

2. Mix in the first portion of powdered sugar.

3. Add the almond flour.

4. Add the bitter-almond extract, vanilla, and orange zest.

5. Mix into a uniform dough.

6. Cover directly with plastic wrap.

7. Refrigerate overnight.

8. The next day, preheat the oven to 320°F.

9. Dust the work surface with some of the finishing powdered sugar.

10. Transfer the dough to the surface.

11. Shape into an even log.

12. Cut into 18 slices.

13. Shape each slice into an oval about 3/8 inch thick.

14. Coat each cookie generously with powdered sugar.

15. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

16. Bake for about 18 minutes.

17. The cookies should remain pale and soft in the center.

18. Cool completely before moving.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Do not wait for the cookies to become firm in the oven; they set as they cool.

title: Cavallucci Senesi
instructions:
Cavallucci Senesi

Rustic Siena cookies with walnuts, candied orange, anise, honey, and warm spices.

Yield: about 20 cookies

2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
1/2 cup plus 1 tbsp granulated sugar
1/2 cup water

1 1/2 tsp baker's ammonia
2 tsp anise seeds
1 tbsp mixed cinnamon, nutmeg, and ground cloves

Preparation

1. Put the main portion of flour in a bowl.

2. Add the spices, baker's ammonia, anise seeds, pepper, and salt.

3. Coarsely chop the walnuts.

4. Finely dice the candied orange.

5. Add both to the flour.

6. Put the water, sugar, and honey in a saucepan.

7. Heat until the sugar dissolves and the syrup is very hot.

8. Pour the syrup over the dry ingredients.

9. Mix into a soft workable dough.

10. Rest for 30 minutes.

11. Preheat a conventional oven to 340°F.

12. Dust the work surface with the remaining flour.

13. Divide the dough into about 20 pieces.

14. Shape into small balls.

15. Flatten each slightly in the center.

16. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

17. Bake for 14–15 minutes.

18. Cool completely.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Cavallucci should remain slightly soft in the center; overbaking makes them hard.

title: Schiacciata alla Fiorentina
instructions:
Schiacciata alla Fiorentina

Soft Florentine Carnival cake flavored with orange and saffron.

Yield: 12 servings

Ingredients

2 large eggs
1/2 cup granulated sugar
2/3 cup neutral oil
2 3/4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
1/3 cup whole milk
1 pinch saffron
juice and finely grated zest of 1 orange
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp vanilla baking powder
1/3 tsp fine salt
1/3 cup powdered vanilla sugar for finishing
2 tsp oil for the pan
2 tbsp flour for the pan

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 400°F.

2. Oil and flour a rectangular pan about 9 × 12 inches.

3. Separate the egg yolks and whites.

4. Put the yolks in a large bowl.

5. Add the sugar.

6. Beat until pale and foamy.

7. Slowly add the oil.

8. Gradually mix in the flour.

9. Add the milk.

10. Add the saffron.

11. Add the orange juice and zest.

12. Mix until smooth.

13. Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks.

14. Fold them in gently.

15. Add the baking powder and salt.

16. Mix gently.

17. Pour into the pan.

18. Smooth the surface.

19. Bake for about 30 minutes.

20. Test with a toothpick.

21. Cool completely.

22. Dust generously with powdered vanilla sugar.

Service

Cut into squares and serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Schiacciata should remain low and airy, so use a broad shallow pan rather than a deep cake pan.

title: Florentine Zuccotto
instructions:
Florentine Zuccotto

Florentine semifreddo lined with sponge cake and filled with saffron cream and chocolate.

Yield: 8–10 servings

Ingredients

For the sponge cake
7 small eggs
1 1/4 cups granulated sugar
2 cups all-purpose flour
3 1/2 tbsp melted butter
2 tsp butter for the pan
2 tbsp flour for the pan

For the syrup
1 cup water
1 2/3 cups granulated sugar
2 tbsp plus 2 tsp brandy or rum

For the filling
about 2/3 cup chopped dark chocolate, divided
1 2/3 cups heavy cream
a generous pinch saffron threads
1/4 cup plus 1 tbsp granulated sugar

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 375°F.

2. Butter and flour a 9 1/2-inch cake pan.

3. Put the eggs and sugar in a saucepan.

4. Heat over medium heat while stirring to 122°F.

5. Transfer to a large bowl.

6. Beat for 15–20 minutes, until very voluminous.

7. Sift the flour.

8. Fold it in gently.

9. Mix 1 tablespoon batter into the melted butter.

10. Fold this mixture back into the batter.

11. Pour into the pan.

12. Bake for 20–25 minutes.

13. Cool completely.

14. Unmold.

15. Cut the sponge into strips.

16. Line a roughly 2-quart hemispherical bowl with the strips, leaving no gaps.

17. For the syrup, put the water and sugar in a saucepan.

18. Heat until dissolved.

19. Cool completely.

20. Add the liquor.

21. Brush the cake with syrup.

22. Melt about 1/4 cup of the chocolate.

23. Brush it over the cake lining.

24. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

25. Heat 3 tablespoons cream with the saffron.

26. Infuse for 1 hour.

27. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

28. Chop the remaining chocolate.

29. Whip the remaining cream with the sugar.

30. Add the chilled saffron cream.

31. Continue whipping to firm peaks.

32. Fold in the chopped chocolate.

33. Fill the bowl, leaving about 3/8 inch at the top.

34. Cover with the remaining sponge strips.

35. Brush with more syrup.

36. Cover.

37. Freeze for at least 6 hours.

38. Remove from the freezer at least 30 minutes before serving.

39. Invert onto a platter.

Service

Cut into wedges and serve semifrozen.

Chef's note

The thin chocolate layer acts as a barrier and prevents the cream from over-soaking the sponge.

title: Tuscan Castagnaccio
instructions:
Tuscan Castagnaccio

Tuscan chestnut-flour cake with raisins, pine nuts, walnuts, rosemary, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

1/3 cup raisins
1 tbsp Vin Santo
2 cups chestnut flour
1 2/3 cups water
1/3 tsp fine salt
3 tbsp pine nuts
about 1/2 cup chopped walnuts
1 rosemary sprig
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

2. Put the raisins in a bowl.

3. Cover with warm water.

4. Add the Vin Santo.

5. Soak for 15 minutes.

6. Drain and dry.

7. Put the chestnut flour and salt in a large bowl.

8. Gradually whisk in the water.

9. Continue until smooth and lump-free.

10. Add the raisins.

11. Add half of the pine nuts and half of the walnuts.

12. Stir.

13. Grease a 9 1/2-inch round pan with 1 tablespoon olive oil.

14. Pour in the batter.

15. Scatter the remaining pine nuts and walnuts over the top.

16. Strip the rosemary leaves from the sprig.

17. Scatter them over the surface.

18. Drizzle with the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil.

19. Bake for 25–30 minutes.

20. Remove when the surface is dry with fine cracks.

21. Cool slightly.

Service

Serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

Castagnaccio should not be thick; a relatively shallow layer creates the traditional cracked surface and texture.

title: Torta della Nonna
instructions:
Torta della Nonna

Tuscan shortcrust tart filled with lemon pastry cream and topped with pine nuts.

Yield: 1 10-inch tart

Ingredients

For the shortcrust pastry
2 3/4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
10 1/2 tbsp butter
3/4 cup granulated sugar
1 large egg
1 egg yolk
2 tsp baking powder
1 tbsp limoncello cream liqueur

For the pastry cream
3 cups plus 3 tbsp whole milk
4 large eggs
5 tbsp granulated sugar
2 tbsp cornstarch or all-purpose flour
1–2 tbsp limoncello cream liqueur or 1 packet vanilla sugar

For finishing
about 1/3 cup pine nuts
1/4 cup powdered sugar
2 tsp butter for the pan

Preparation

1. Put the flour, butter, sugar, egg, yolk, baking powder, and limoncello cream liqueur in a food processor.

2. Pulse until the dough comes together.

3. Shape into a disk.

4. Wrap in plastic.

5. Refrigerate while making the pastry cream.

6. Heat the milk until just below boiling.

7. In a saucepan, whisk the eggs with the sugar.

8. Add the cornstarch or flour.

9. Whisk until smooth.

10. Gradually add the hot milk while whisking.

11. Add the limoncello cream liqueur or vanilla.

12. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until thick.

13. Do not allow it to boil vigorously.

14. Transfer to a bowl.

15. Cover directly with plastic wrap.

16. Refrigerate until cold.

17. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

18. Butter a 10-inch tart pan.

19. Divide the pastry into two portions, one slightly larger.

20. Roll out the larger portion.

21. Line the bottom and sides of the pan.

22. Prick the bottom.

23. Add the cold pastry cream.

24. Smooth the surface.

25. Roll the remaining pastry between two sheets of parchment.

26. Cover the tart.

27. Trim and seal the edges with a fork.

28. Lightly prick the top.

29. Scatter the pine nuts evenly over the surface.

30. Bake for 30–40 minutes, preventing the surface from becoming too dark.

31. Cool completely.

32. Dust with powdered sugar.

Service

Serve at room temperature or slightly cool.

Chef's note

The pastry cream should be completely cold before it is enclosed in the crust so the base keeps a cleaner structure.

Brigidini di Lamporecchio

Thin Tuscan anise wafers, crisp and light.

Yield: about 30 wafers

1 cup cake flour
2/3 cup granulated sugar
3 large eggs
1 tbsp anise seeds
1 pinch fine salt
1/4 tsp vanilla extract, optional

Preparation

1. Heat a traditional brigidini iron or a flat wafer iron.

2. Put the eggs in a bowl.

3. Beat until foamy.

4. Add the sugar.

5. Continue beating until uniform.

6. Add the anise seeds.

7. Mix in the flour.

8. Add the salt.

9. Add the vanilla if using.

10. Mix into a smooth soft dough.

11. Scoop 1 teaspoon dough.

12. Place it in the center of the hot iron.

13. Close the iron immediately.

14. Cook for only a few seconds, until dry and lightly golden.

15. Open the iron.

16. Remove the wafer carefully.

17. Cool on a rack.

18. Repeat with the remaining dough.

Brigidini become crisp as they cool, so do not cook them until dark.

title: Buccellato di Lucca
instructions:
Buccellato di Lucca

Lucca sweet yeast bread with raisins and anise seeds.

Yield: 1 large loaf

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
3/4 cup granulated sugar

about 1 1/2 tbsp fresh yeast
2 large eggs, divided
1 cup warm whole milk
1/3 cup dried muscat raisins
2 tsp anise seeds
1/2 tsp fine salt
2 tbsp granulated sugar for the top

Preparation

1. Soak the raisins in warm water for 15 minutes.

2. Drain and dry thoroughly.

3. Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk.

4. Put the flour in a large bowl.

5. Add the sugar and salt.

6. Add 1 egg.

7. Add the softened butter.

8. Gradually add the yeast milk.

9. Knead until smooth and elastic.

10. If needed, add only 1–2 tablespoons warm water to bring the dough together.

11. Work in the raisins and anise seeds.

12. Shape into a ball.

13. Cover.

14. Let rise until doubled, about 2 hours.

15. Shape into a large loaf or ring.

16. Put on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

17. Cover.

18. Let rise again for 45–60 minutes.

19. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

20. Beat the remaining egg with the topping sugar.

21. Brush the surface.

22. Bake for about 1 hour.

23. If the top becomes too dark, loosely cover with foil during the final 15 minutes.

24. Cool completely on a rack.

Service

Slice and serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Dry the raisins thoroughly before adding them so they do not make the dough sticky.

12. Cook the second side for 1–2 minutes.

13. Transfer to a plate.

15. Put about 3 tablespoons ricotta in the center of each neccio while still warm.

The batter should flow easily without becoming watery; adding the water gradually accommodates differences in chestnut flour absorption.

5. Rest for 30 minutes.

9. Gradually roll to about 1/16 inch thick.

12. Heat the oil to 340°F.

title: Torcolo di San Costanzo
instructions:
Torcolo di San Costanzo

Perugia yeast ring bread with candied citron, raisins, pine nuts, and anise.

Yield: 1 ring

Ingredients

5 cups all-purpose flour
1 cup granulated sugar
about 2/3 cup diced candied citron

Preparation

1. Soak the raisins in warm water for 15 minutes.

2. Drain and squeeze dry.

3. Put the flour and salt in a large bowl.

4. Dissolve the yeast in 1/4 cup of the warm water.

5. Add it to the flour.

Umbrian Rocciata

Umbrian rolled pastry filled with apples, walnuts, raisins, figs, pine nuts, cocoa, candied citron, and spices.

1 tsp ground cinnamon
1 tsp ground cloves

Preparation

2. Add the olive oil and wine.

4. Cover.

6. Soak the raisins in warm water for 15 minutes.

Perugia Pinoccate

Ciaramicola

Perugia Easter ring cake flavored with Alchermes and topped with white meringue icing and colored sprinkles.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

For the cake
4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
1 cup granulated sugar
4 large eggs
about 1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp Alchermes
7 tbsp softened butter
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp baking powder
1 tsp finely grated lemon zest
1/3 tsp fine salt

For the icing
2 egg whites
1 1/4 cups powdered sugar
about 1/4 cup colored sprinkles

Preparation

1. Preheat a conventional oven to 340°F.

2. Butter and flour a 9 1/2–10-inch ring mold.

3. Put the eggs in a large bowl.

4. Add the sugar.

5. Beat until pale and fluffy.

6. Add the softened butter.

7. Add the Alchermes.

8. Add the lemon zest and salt.

9. Sift together the flour and baking powder.

10. Add them in several additions.

11. Pour into the mold.

12. Smooth the surface.

13. Bake for 40–45 minutes.

14. Test with a toothpick.

15. Cool completely.

16. Unmold.

17. Put the icing egg whites in a clean bowl.

18. Beat to stiff peaks.

19. Gradually add the powdered sugar.

20. Continue until glossy and firm.

21. Pour the icing over the cold cake.

22. Let it drip naturally down the sides.

23. Immediately scatter the colored sprinkles over the icing.

24. Let the icing dry completely.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

The cake must be completely cold before icing or the meringue will melt and lose volume.

Umbrian Saffron Tozzetti

Twice-baked Umbrian cookies with hazelnuts, almonds, mistrà, lemon, and Cascia saffron.

1 1/4 cups hazelnuts

finely grated zest of 1 lemon
about 3 tbsp powdered or finely crumbled Cascia saffron

Preparation

1. Put the saffron in a small cup.

2. Add the hot water.

3. Infuse for at least 2 hours.

4. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

5. Sift the flour onto a work surface.

6. Add the sugar and baking soda.

7. Make a well.

8. Add the lemon zest, eggs, yolks, lard, and mistrà.

9. Add the saffron with all of its soaking water.

10. Knead until uniform.

11. Add the almonds and hazelnuts.

12. Work until evenly distributed.

13. Divide the dough into 3 portions.

14. Shape into 3 logs.

17. Remove from the oven.

The long saffron infusion extracts its color and aroma more evenly before it enters the dough.

instructions:
Crescionda Spoletina

Traditional Spoleto three-layer dessert with amaretti, chocolate, milk, cinnamon, and mistrà.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

6 large eggs
3/4 cup granulated sugar
2 tbsp all-purpose flour
2 tbsp mistrà
finely grated zest of 1 lemon
1 tsp ground cinnamon
about 1 cup chopped dark chocolate
about 2 1/4 cups crushed amaretti
6 1/3 cups whole milk
1 tbsp butter for the pan
2 tbsp flour for the pan
1/4 cup powdered sugar for finishing

Preparation

1. Preheat a conventional oven to 320°F.

2. Butter and flour a 9 1/2-inch cake pan.

3. Finely chop the dark chocolate.

4. Finely crush the amaretti.

5. Combine the chocolate and amaretti in a large bowl.

6. Add the flour, cinnamon, and lemon zest.

7. Mix.

8. Put the eggs and sugar in a second bowl.

9. Beat until pale and foamy.

10. Gradually add the milk while mixing.

11. Pour the liquids over the chocolate-and-amaretti mixture.

12. Mix gently until no lumps remain.

13. Add the mistrà.

14. Mix again.

15. Pour into the prepared pan.

16. Bake for about 20 minutes, until the surface is set while the center remains soft.

17. Cool until warm.

18. Cool completely.

19. Dust with powdered sugar.

Service

Serve at room temperature or slightly cool.

Chef's note

The very fluid batter is intentional; its characteristic layers form naturally during baking.

Marche Frustingo

Rich Marche fruit cake with dried figs, raisins, honey, nuts, chocolate, and citrus.

about 1/2 cup assorted candied fruit for decorating

Preparation

1. The night before, cut the figs into small pieces.

2. Put the figs and raisins in a large bowl.

3. Add about 1 2/3 cups white wine.

4. Cover.

5. Soak overnight.

6. The next day, drain, reserving the soaking wine.

7. Coarsely chop the hazelnuts and walnuts.

8. Chop the chocolate.

9. In a large bowl, combine the sugar, whole-wheat flour, breadcrumbs, honey, nutmeg, and citrus zest.

10. Add the hazelnuts, walnuts, figs, raisins, chocolate, and candied citron.

11. Add the olive oil.

12. Mix thoroughly.

13. Gradually add up to about 1/2 cup of the reserved soaking wine, only until the mixture is very thick but workable.

14. Preheat the oven to 320°F.

15. Oil and flour a 10-inch pan.

16. Add the mixture.

17. Smooth and compact gently.

18. Bake for about 40 minutes.

19. Rest in the pan for 10 minutes.

20. Unmold onto a rack.

21. Cool completely.

22. Decorate with the assorted candied fruit.

Service

Serve at room temperature, preferably after several hours of resting.

Chef's note

Add the reserved wine gradually after soaking because the amount needed depends on how much liquid the figs absorbed.

Marche Cicerchiata

Carnival sweet made from tiny fried dough balls bound with honey, sugar, and almonds.

For finishing

Preparation

1. Put the flour, sugar, butter, eggs, yolks, anise liqueur, lemon zest, and salt in a mixer bowl.

2. Knead until uniform.

3. Transfer to a work surface.

4. Knead briefly by hand.

5. Divide into portions.

6. Roll into ropes about 3/8 inch thick.

7. Cut into chickpea-size pieces.

8. Heat the oil to 330°F.

9. Fry only a few at a time until golden, about 1–2 minutes.

10. Drain thoroughly.

11. Put the honey and finishing sugar in a wide saucepan.

12. Heat over medium heat until the sugar dissolves.

13. Add the fried dough balls.

14. Add the almonds.

15. Stir quickly until everything is coated.

16. Transfer to a lightly greased ring mold or shape into a wreath on a platter.

17. Press gently with a damp spoon.

18. Immediately decorate with the sprinkles.

Chef's note

Add the fried dough balls while the honey mixture is very hot because it thickens quickly as it cools.

Resting the filling for 24 hours lets the breadcrumbs absorb the grape must, coffee, and liqueur so the filling stays stable during baking.

Abruzzo Pizza Dolce

Abruzzo layer cake with pastry cream, chocolate cream, almond cream, rum and Alchermes syrups, and royal icing.

1/3 cup rum

2 tsp granulated sugar

For the Alchermes syrup
1/3 cup Alchermes
2 tbsp water
1 tsp granulated sugar

For decorating
1/3 cup sliced almonds
1/4 cup colored sprinkles

Preparation

1. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

2. Butter and flour a roughly 12-inch cake pan.

3. Beat the 8 eggs with the sugar for at least 15–20 minutes.

4. Sift together the flour and potato starch.

5. Fold them in gently.

6. Pour into the pan.

7. Bake for about 45 minutes without opening the oven during the first 35 minutes.

8. Test with a toothpick.

9. Cool completely.

10. For the pastry cream, beat 4 yolks with the sugar and flour.

11. Heat the milk with the lemon peel.

12. Remove the peel.

13. Gradually whisk the hot milk into the yolk mixture.

14. Cook over low heat, stirring, until thick.

15. Transfer to a bowl and cool covered directly on the surface.

16. For the chocolate cream, repeat with the remaining yolks, milk, sugar, and flour.

17. At the end of cooking, add the chopped chocolate.

18. Stir until melted.

19. Cool covered directly on the surface.

20. For the almond cream, bring the water and sugar to a boil.

21. Gradually add the almonds.

22. Cook, stirring, until soft and slightly grainy.

23. Cool.

24. Mix the rum-syrup ingredients in one bowl.

25. Mix the Alchermes-syrup ingredients in another bowl.

26. Cut the sponge into 3 equal layers.

27. Moisten the first layer with the rum syrup.

28. Spread with chocolate cream.

29. Spread the almond cream over it.

30. Add the second layer.

31. Moisten with Alchermes syrup.

32. Spread with pastry cream.

33. Moisten the inner side of the third layer with Alchermes.

34. Place it upside down on the cake.

35. Moisten the top with the rum syrup.

36. Cover.

37. Refrigerate for at least 12 hours.

38. For the icing, beat the egg whites with the lemon juice.

39. Gradually add the powdered sugar.

40. Continue until smooth and firm.

41. Cover the entire cake.

42. Decorate with the sliced almonds and sprinkles.

43. Let the icing set before serving.

Service

Serve cold.

Chef's note

The overnight rest allows the syrups and three creams to balance and makes the cake easier to slice cleanly.

3. Knead vigorously until smooth and uniform.

5. Divide the dough into pieces.

8. Heat the peanut oil to 350°F.
9. Fry only a few pieces at a time until golden.
10. Drain on paper towels.
11. Put the honey and sugar in a large saucepan.
12. Heat over medium heat until the sugar dissolves and the honey is very fluid.
13. Add the fried pieces and almonds.
14. Stir quickly until everything is coated.

18. Cool completely.

1 cup mixed candied fruit

For finishing

1/3 cup powdered sugar

Preparation

1. Mound the flour on a work surface.
2. Add the sugar, softened butter, and vanilla.

5. Shape into a disk, cover, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
6. Put the cooked wheat, milk, and butter in a saucepan.

8. Cool completely.
9. Work the ricotta until smooth.

11. Separate the 6 eggs.
12. Mix the yolks into the ricotta.
13. Add the orange-blossom flavoring and candied fruit.

16. Add the cold cooked-wheat cream.
17. Preheat the oven to 350°F.
18. Butter and flour a 10 1/2–11-inch pan.
19. Roll out about two-thirds of the pastry.
20. Line the bottom and sides of the pan.
21. Prick the bottom.
22. Add the filling.
23. Roll out the remaining pastry.
24. Cut strips and arrange the traditional lattice over the top.
25. Bake for about 60 minutes.
26. Turn off the oven and leave the tart inside for 1 hour with the door slightly open.
27. Cool completely.
28. Dust with powdered sugar.

Pastiera improves after a long rest because the ricotta, wheat, and orange-blossom flavors meld together.

title: Sfogliatella Riccia
instructions:
Sfogliatella Riccia

Neapolitan layered pastry filled with semolina, ricotta, candied fruit, vanilla, and cinnamon.

Yield: about 12 pastries

Ingredients

For the pastry
4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp water
1 tbsp honey
3/4 tsp fine salt
about 1 cup plus 2 tbsp softened lard for laminating

For the filling
3/4 cup semolina
1/2 cup well-drained ricotta
1/2 cup plus 2 tbsp granulated sugar
1 medium egg
1 1/2 cups water
1/3 cup mixed candied fruit
1 vial vanilla flavoring
1 pinch ground cinnamon
1/3 tsp fine salt

For finishing
1/3 cup powdered sugar

Preparation

1. Mound the flour on a work surface.
2. Dissolve the honey and salt in the warm water.
3. Gradually add the water to the flour.
4. Work into a very firm, initially rough dough.
5. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
6. Knead again until smooth.
7. Brush lightly with lard.
8. Rest for 1 hour.
9. Roll the dough into an extremely long, paper-thin strip without using flour.
10. Spread softened lard over the entire surface.
11. Roll very tightly into a cylinder about 2 1/2 inches wide.
12. Coat the outside lightly with lard.
13. Wrap in plastic.
14. Refrigerate for at least 12 hours.
15. For the filling, bring the water and salt to a boil.
16. Gradually whisk in the semolina.
17. Cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until very thick.
18. Cool completely.
19. Mix the ricotta, sugar, egg, candied fruit, vanilla, and cinnamon.
20. Mix in the cold semolina.
21. Cut the pastry cylinder into slices about 3/8 inch thick.
22. Lightly grease each slice with lard.
23. Push the center outward with your thumbs while rotating the edges to form a shell with the layers facing outward.
24. Fill with about 2 tablespoons filling.
25. Bring the edges close together without sealing completely.
26. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
27. Preheat the oven to 350°F.
28. Bake for about 20–25 minutes, until deeply golden.
29. Cool slightly.
30. Dust with powdered sugar.

Service

Serve warm.

Chef's note

The layered structure depends on two things: paper-thin dough and evenly distributed lard before rolling.

title: Neapolitan Babà
instructions:
Neapolitan Babà

Neapolitan yeast cakes enriched with butter and eggs and soaked in rum syrup.

Yield: 10 babà

Ingredients

For the dough
2 cups all-purpose flour
5 1/2 tbsp softened butter
3 tbsp granulated sugar
4 large eggs
about 1 1/2 tbsp fresh yeast
2/3 tsp fine salt

For the syrup
1 1/4 cups water
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp granulated sugar
2/3 cup rum

For the molds
3 1/2 tbsp butter

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in 1 tablespoon warm water.
2. Put the flour and sugar in a large bowl.
3. Add the yeast.
4. Add the eggs one at a time.
5. Work vigorously, repeatedly lifting and slapping the dough.
6. Add the salt.
7. Gradually add the softened butter.
8. Continue mixing until elastic and visibly bubbly.
9. Cover.
10. Let rise in the same bowl for about 40 minutes.
11. Butter 10 babà molds.
12. Fill them halfway with dough.
13. Cover.
14. Let rise until the dough approaches the rim.
15. Preheat the oven to 350°F.
16. Bake for at least 15 minutes, until deeply golden.
17. Unmold.
18. Cool completely.
19. For the syrup, bring the water and sugar to a boil.
20. Boil for 2 minutes.
21. Remove from the heat.
22. Dip each babà in the hot syrup, turning to soak every side.
23. Drain briefly.
24. Arrange on a platter.
25. Shortly before serving, drizzle evenly with the rum.
26. Cover with a clean towel.
27. Rest for 10 minutes.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

The babà should be completely cool before soaking in hot syrup so it absorbs the liquid without falling apart.

Struffoli

Preparation

1. Mound the flour on a work surface and make a well.
2. Add the eggs, butter, sugar, liqueur, lemon zest, and salt.
3. Knead until smooth.
4. Shape into a ball.
5. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
6. Knead briefly again.
7. Divide into small portions.
8. Roll each into a rope about finger-thick.
9. Cut into small pieces.
10. Arrange on a lightly floured towel.
11. Sift or shake off excess flour.
12. Heat the oil to 350°F.
13. Fry only a few at a time until puffed and golden.
14. Drain on paper towels.
15. Warm the honey over a water bath until very fluid.
16. Remove from the heat.
17. Add the struffoli.
18. Toss gently.
19. Add half of the sprinkles and half of the candied fruit.
20. Put a jar in the center of a serving platter.
21. Arrange the struffoli around it in a wreath.
22. Decorate with the remaining sprinkles and candied fruit.
23. Let the honey set.
24. Remove the jar.

Removing excess flour before frying keeps the oil cleaner and prevents the struffoli from darkening.

instructions:
Delizia al Limone

Sorrento lemon dessert made with soft sponge domes, lemon pastry cream, whipped cream, and limoncello syrup.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the sponge domes
5 large eggs
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp granulated sugar
about 3/4 cup plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
2 cups plus 2 tbsp lemon juice

For the syrup
2 cups plus 2 tbsp water
1 1/4 cups granulated sugar
1/4 cup limoncello or Benevento liqueur

For the pastry cream
3 cups plus 3 tbsp whole milk
3 egg yolks
1 cup plus 2 tbsp granulated sugar
1 cup all-purpose flour

For the sauce and decoration
about 3 cups prepared pastry cream
4 1/4 cups heavy cream, divided
finely grated zest of 3 lemons
about 1/2 cup cold milk, for thinning
about 1/4 cup candied lemon peel for decorating

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.
2. Separate the eggs.
3. Beat the yolks with the sugar and about half of one egg white.
4. Beat the remaining whites while gradually adding the lemon juice.
5. Sift the flour.
6. Fold it gently into the yolks.
7. Fold in the egg whites with a spatula.
8. Pipe half-sphere sponge domes onto two parchment-lined baking sheets.
9. Bake at 350°F.
10. When they begin to color, reduce the oven to 320°F.
11. Continue baking to about 30 minutes total, until dry.
12. Cool completely.
13. For the syrup, bring the water and sugar to a boil.
14. Cook until the sugar dissolves and the syrup thickens slightly.
15. Cool.
16. Add the limoncello.
17. For the pastry cream, heat the milk.
18. Beat the yolks with the sugar.
19. Add the flour.
20. Gradually add the hot milk.
21. Cook, stirring, until thick.
22. Cool completely.
23. Whip about 3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp cream.
24. Add the zest of 3 lemons to the pastry cream.
25. Divide the pastry cream in half.
26. Fold the whipped cream into one half.
27. Fill the sponge domes with this cream, joining two half-domes for each dessert.
28. Dip each dessert briefly in the syrup.
29. Recombine the two portions of pastry cream.
30. Gradually add cold milk until fluid but still coating.
31. Whip the remaining cream.
32. Fold half of it into the sauce.
33. Coat the delizie with the sauce.
34. Decorate with the remaining whipped cream and candied lemon peel.
35. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

Service

Serve well chilled.

Chef's note

The coating sauce should flow evenly while remaining thick enough to cling to each dessert.

instructions:
Zeppole di San Giuseppe

Neapolitan fried choux rings filled with pastry cream and topped with syruped sour cherries.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

For the zeppole
2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
6 large eggs
about 1 cup plus 2 tbsp lard

Preparation

1. Put the lard, sugar, and water in a saucepan.
2. Heat until nearly boiling.
3. Gradually add the flour.
4. Add the salt.
5. Stir continuously until uniform and pulling away from the pan.
6. Remove from the heat.
7. Cool for 5 minutes.
8. Add the eggs one at a time, fully incorporating each one.
9. Transfer to a pastry bag fitted with a star tip.
10. Pipe rings onto squares of parchment.
11. Heat the peanut oil to about 330°F in one pan.
12. Heat the rendered lard to about 350°F in a second pan.
13. Lower one zeppola with its paper into the first pan.

15. Fry until puffed and lightly golden.

17. Finish frying until deeply golden.
18. Drain on paper towels.
19. Repeat with the remaining zeppole.
20. For the pastry cream, heat the milk with the lemon peel and vanilla.
21. Mix the yolks, sugar, flour, and potato starch.
22. Gradually add the hot milk.
23. Cook, stirring, until thick and smooth.
24. Remove the lemon and vanilla.
25. Cool completely.
26. Fill the zeppole with pastry cream using a pastry bag.
27. Top each with syruped sour cherries.
28. Dust with powdered sugar.

Chef's note

The traditional two-stage fry lets the zeppole expand slowly before developing their final golden crust.

8. Roll the dough very thinly.

Overnight drying helps the rosettes hold their shape during frying.

Pasticciotto Leccese

Salento shortcrust pastries made with lard and filled with pastry cream.

Yield: about 15 pastries

4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
about 1 cup plus 2 tbsp lard

seeds from 1 vanilla bean

1/3 tsp fine salt

For the pastry cream
4 1/4 cups whole milk
6 egg yolks

1 2/3 cups granulated sugar

For finishing
1 beaten egg

Preparation

1. Mix the sugar and lard without whipping.
2. Add the 4 egg yolks.
3. Mix in the flour.
4. Add the vanilla, lemon zest, and salt.
5. Work only until uniform.
6. Shape into a disk.
7. Wrap in plastic.
8. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
9. For the pastry cream, beat the 6 yolks with the sugar.
10. Add the sifted flour.
11. Add 1/2 cup milk and mix until smooth.
12. Heat the remaining milk.
13. Pour the yolk mixture into the hot milk.
14. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until boiling and thick.
15. Transfer to a glass container.
16. Cover directly on the surface.
17. Chill completely.
18. Shape the pastry into a cylinder.
19. Cut portions large enough to line the molds.
20. Flatten each portion to about 3/16 inch thick.
21. Line the bottoms and sides of the molds.
22. Fill with cold pastry cream, leaving about 3/16 inch below the rim.
23. Roll more pastry slightly thinner.
24. Cover each mold.
25. Seal the edges into the characteristic domed shape.
26. Refrigerate for about 1 hour.
27. Preheat the oven to 425°F.
28. Brush with beaten egg.
29. Bake for about 10 minutes, until deeply golden.
30. Cool for 2 minutes.
31. Unmold carefully.

Serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

The pastry cream should be completely cold before filling the pastry so the crust does not soften before baking.

Sporcamuss

Puglian puff-pastry squares filled with diplomat cream and served warm.

Yield: 10 pastries

2 egg yolks
2/3 cup plus 1 tbsp whole milk
1/4 cup granulated sugar
2 1/2 tbsp cornstarch
seeds from 1/2 vanilla bean
scant 1/2 cup heavy cream
3 tbsp powdered sugar

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

2. For the cream, beat the egg yolks with the granulated sugar until pale.

3. Heat the milk with the vanilla seeds and pod for about 10 minutes.

4. Remove the pod.

5. Gradually whisk the hot milk into the yolks.

6. Add the cornstarch.

7. Whisk until completely smooth.

8. Transfer to a saucepan.

9. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until thick.

10. Transfer to a bowl.

11. Cover directly on the surface.

12. Cool completely.

13. Whip the heavy cream with the powdered sugar.

14. Fold it gently into the cold pastry cream.

15. Cut the puff pastry into 20 equal squares.

16. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

17. Prick with a fork.

18. Sprinkle with the granulated sugar.

19. Bake for 10–15 minutes, until deeply golden.

20. Cool.

21. Pipe or spoon the cream onto 10 squares.

22. Cover with the remaining 10 squares.

23. Just before serving, warm in a 210°F oven for 3–4 minutes.

24. Dust with powdered sugar.

Service

Serve warm.

Chef's note

The pastry cream must be completely cold before folding in the whipped cream so the filling stays stable and light.

Sicilian Cannoli

6. Cut into even rectangles.

21. Brush with more syrup.

23. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.

27. Cover the top and sides.

instructions:
Sicilian Lemon Granita

Sicilian lemon granita with a fine crystalline texture.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

2 cups plus 2 tbsp water
1 cup fresh strained lemon juice
1 cup granulated sugar
yellow peel of 1 organic lemon, optional

Preparation

1. Wash and dry the lemons.

2. If using, remove thin strips of peel without the white pith.

3. Put the water and sugar in a saucepan.

4. Heat gently until the sugar dissolves completely.

5. Add the peel.

6. Simmer for 3–5 minutes.

7. Turn off the heat.

8. Remove the peel.

9. Cool completely, first at room temperature and then in the refrigerator.

10. Juice the lemons.

11. Strain the juice.

12. Add it to the cold syrup.

13. Mix thoroughly.

14. Pour into a wide shallow metal container.

15. Freeze for 30–40 minutes.

16. Remove from the freezer.

17. Break up the ice crystals with a fork and stir vigorously.

18. Return to the freezer.

19. Repeat every 30 minutes for 3–4 hours, until fine and uniform.

Service

Serve in well-chilled glasses or dishes.

Chef's note

Frequent stirring during freezing prevents large ice crystals from forming.

title: Brioche Col Tuppo
instructions:
Brioche Col Tuppo

Soft Sicilian brioche with the characteristic top knot, traditionally served with granita or gelato.

Yield: about 12 brioche

Ingredients

8 1/3 cups bread flour
1 2/3 cups water
scant 1/2 cup whole milk
about 1/3 cup fresh yeast
1/2 cup granulated sugar
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt
5 tbsp softened butter
2 egg yolks

For brushing
1 egg yolk
1 tsp whole milk

Preparation

1. Put the flour, sugar, and crumbled yeast in a mixer bowl.

2. Mix with the dough hook.

3. Add about one-third of the water.

4. Add the first egg yolk.

5. Once absorbed, add the second.

6. Mix for about 1 minute.

7. Gradually add more water.

8. Add the salt.

9. Slowly add the remaining water.

10. Add the milk.

11. Add the softened butter a little at a time.

12. Knead until smooth, elastic, and fully developed.

13. Cover.

14. Rest for 30 minutes.

15. Divide into portions about 1/3 cup in size for the main brioche.

16. Reserve some dough for the top knots.

17. Round the large pieces into smooth balls.

18. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

19. Form smaller balls for the top knots.

20. Make an indentation in the center of each brioche.

21. Insert one small ball into each indentation.

22. Proof at 75–79°F for about 2 hours, until doubled.

23. Preheat a conventional oven to 400°F.

24. Mix the yolk and milk.

25. Brush gently.

26. Bake for 5 minutes at 400°F.

27. Reduce the oven to 375°F.

28. Continue baking for about 15 minutes.

29. Cool on a rack.

Service

Serve at room temperature or slightly warm.

Chef's note

Push the top knot deeply into the indentation so it stays attached during proofing.

Sicilian Buccellato

Sicilian shortcrust ring filled with nuts, jam, chocolate, candied fruit, and cinnamon.

Chilling the filling before shaping makes it easier to enclose without leaking.

title: Emilian Fresh Egg Pasta
instructions:
Emilian Fresh Egg Pasta

Classic Emilia egg pasta rolled by hand with a rolling pin.

Yield: about 4 servings

Ingredients

3 1/3 cups all-purpose flour
4 medium eggs

Preparation

1. Crack the eggs into a bowl.

2. Weigh or check their size for consistency.

3. Sift the flour onto a work surface.

4. Reserve about 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon flour for adjusting the dough.

5. Make a wide well in the flour.

6. Pour the eggs into the center.

7. Beat them with a fork.

8. Gradually draw flour in from the inner walls.

9. Once coarse crumbs form, begin kneading by hand.

10. Knead vigorously for 10–15 minutes.

11. Add only a little of the reserved flour if the dough remains sticky.

12. Stop when smooth, soft, elastic, and no longer sticky.

13. Shape into a ball.

14. Wrap in plastic or place in a food-safe bag.

15. Rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.

16. Clean the work surface.

17. Dust it very lightly with flour.

18. Flatten the dough by hand.

19. Roll from the center outward.

20. Rotate the sheet frequently.

21. Continue until it reaches the thickness required for the pasta being made.

Chef's note

Resting relaxes the gluten and makes the dough easier to roll without springing back.

Bolognese Pasta Sheet

Yield: about 10 portions of pasta dough

Preparation

1. Sift the flour onto a work surface.

2. Make a wide well.

3. Crack the eggs into the center.

4. Break the yolks with a fork.

5. Beat the eggs while gradually drawing in flour from the sides.

6. Once the mixture becomes firm enough, begin kneading by hand.

7. Knead vigorously until soft, uniform, and elastic.

8. For green pasta, mix the very well-squeezed chopped spinach into the eggs before fully incorporating the flour.

9. Shape into a ball.

10. Cover with plastic wrap.

12. Dust the work surface very lightly with flour.

13. Flatten the dough.

14. Roll from the center outward.

15. Rotate the sheet frequently.

16. Continue rolling while keeping it as round as possible.

17. Add only enough flour to prevent sticking.

18. Stop when the sheet is thin and even.

Service

Use immediately for tortellini, tagliatelle, lasagne, or other Bolognese pasta.

Chef's note

A properly rolled sfoglia should be elastic, even, and thin without becoming fragile.

Tagliatelle Dough

Letting the sheet dry slightly before cutting prevents the strands from sticking together.

Passatelli Dough

Romagna passatelli made with breadcrumbs, Parmigiano, eggs, lemon, and nutmeg.

3. Skim the surface.

4. Reduce the heat.

5. Simmer for 2–3 hours.

6. Strain the broth.

8. Add the eggs.

13. Wrap.

15. Divide into 2–3 pieces.

16. Bring the strained broth to a boil.

17. Press each piece through a passatelli iron or large-hole potato ricer directly over the broth.

18. Cut the strands about 2–2 1/2 inches long.

19. Cook until they rise to the surface.

20. Simmer for another 30–60 seconds.

Serve immediately in the hot broth.

A well-rested dough holds its shape better when pressed through the iron.

title: Pici Dough
instructions:
Pici Dough

Rustic Tuscan hand-rolled pasta made only with flour, water, and salt.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp type 0 or all-purpose flour
1 cup plus 2 tsp warm water
2/3 tsp fine salt
1/4 cup additional flour for the work surface

Preparation

1. Sift the flour into a large bowl.

2. Make a well in the center.

3. Dissolve the salt in the warm water.

4. Gradually pour the water into the flour.

5. Mix first with a fork.

6. Transfer the dough to a lightly floured work surface.

7. Knead vigorously for 10–12 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

8. Shape into a ball.

9. Wrap in plastic.

10. Rest for 30–40 minutes.

11. Divide the dough into 4 portions.

12. Keep unused portions covered.

13. Roll one portion at a time to about 3/8 inch thick.

14. Cut into strips about 3/8 inch wide.

15. Roll each strip under your palms from the center outward into long even strands about 1/8 inch thick.

16. Arrange on a lightly floured tray without overlapping.

17. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

18. Cook for about 5 minutes, until the pici rise and are tender but still firm.

19. Drain.

Service

Dress immediately with the intended sauce.

Chef's note

Keep unused dough covered at all times so it does not dry and crack while rolling.

Pappardelle Dough

Wide, thin Tuscan egg pasta ribbons.

2 large eggs

13. Let the sheets dry for 5–10 minutes.

14. Roll loosely or fold accordion-style.

15. Cut into ribbons about 1 1/4 inches wide.

16. Unroll immediately.

17. Dust lightly with semolina.

18. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

19. Cook for about 2 minutes.

20. Drain.

Service

Chef's note

Briefly drying the sheets before cutting keeps the wide ribbons from sticking together.

Maremma Tortelli Dough

Tuscan egg-pasta tortelli filled with ricotta and spinach.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the pasta
3 1/3 cups type 0 or all-purpose flour
4 large eggs
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2/3 tsp fine salt

about 1 1/3 cups cooked, squeezed, chopped spinach
1 2/3 cups well-drained ricotta
1 large egg
1/2 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
2/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Put the ricotta in a strainer.

2. Drain for at least 30 minutes.

3. Squeeze the spinach very dry.

4. Chop finely.

5. Combine the ricotta, spinach, and egg in a bowl.

6. Add the Parmigiano, nutmeg, and salt.

7. Mix until uniform.

8. Cover and refrigerate.

9. Make a well in the flour.

10. Crack the 4 eggs into the center.

11. Add the olive oil and salt.

12. Knead for 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

13. Wrap.

14. Rest for 30 minutes.

15. Roll the pasta about 1/16 inch thick.

16. Cut into sheets about 8 inches high.

17. Place about 1 tablespoon filling every 4 inches, about 2 inches from the lower edge.

18. Fold the pasta over the filling.

19. Press around each mound to remove trapped air.

20. Seal firmly.

21. Cut the tortelli with a fluted pastry wheel.

22. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

23. Cook for 3–5 minutes, until the pasta is tender.

24. Lift out with a slotted spoon.

Service

Serve with Tuscan ragù, tomato sauce, or butter and sage.

Chef's note

Both spinach and ricotta must be very dry so the filling does not soften or rupture the pasta.

1 2/3 cups all-purpose flour
1 1/2 cups water
2/3 tsp fine salt
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil for the griddle

1. Sift the flour into a bowl.

2. Add the salt.

3. Gradually add the water.

4. Whisk vigorously until smooth and lump-free.

5. Rest for 20 minutes.

6. Heat a traditional testo or heavy griddle thoroughly.

7. Grease very lightly with the olive oil.

8. Pour in a layer of batter about 1/8 inch thick.

9. Cover with the upper testo plate or a heavy lid.

10. Cook for about 5 minutes, until set and dry.

11. Transfer to a cutting board.

12. Cool slightly.

13. Cut into diamonds or squares about 2 inches wide.

14. Bring a pot of salted water almost to a boil.

15. Turn off the heat.

16. Add the testaroli.

17. Soften for 5 minutes.

18. Drain gently.

Dress with pesto, olive oil and Parmigiano, or Pecorino.

Chef's note

The second cooking water should not boil vigorously or the testaroli can break apart.

19. Cook for 3–5 minutes, or until the pasta rises and is tender but firm.

The dragging motion should be firm but brief so the center hollows without making the pasta too thin.
